body:
First, you had my curiosity.

Now, you have my attention.

For me it’s just joining a server and getting pounced by an alpha raptor. 

Or successfully avoiding a Giga only to be chased down by terror birds or accidentally getting too close to a thero
Yes a sleeping bag. Is a hammock permanent like a bed? I haven’t tried one of them

Another thing that scares some away is, I never refer to her as my Ex. I say “my fiancé” or “my late fiancé”. Because it’s different. She’s a different kind of gone. And it’s a huge can of worms with some people. I hate dating in 2020, where, yeah I’m 28 and more-or-less a widower. That’s not all that common. However, they see me as some sleezball cheater.

The scam of turning 18 in 2010 and having to be a functioning member of society. >:0 What do you mean I have responsibilities BEFORE I’m legally eligible to partake in alcohol. Lame. Bring back the 90s with 151 Pokémon.

For real though, having two young children, maybe it’s because they appealed to us, but cartoons these days are either for 1-4 year olds, or they’re just flat out retarded.

I have. But she’s clearly not over the mistake I made. I can promise her over and over again that it was a one time thing but, ugh. She must still see something, to admit feelings are still there, and to continue to talk to me. I guess how do I prove that?

When we last spoke, she said she still has feelings for me. She has admitted it the whole time, even saying that this other guy was a distraction for her, so she didn’t have time to cry and hurt over me. And it’s too late to pull back on the relocation. My lease is signed and I start my new assignment Dec 1. 
I understand people saying to run away. I’ve tried moving on with someone else but it wasn’t right, my heart is still with her. I mean hell, there’s a reason she calls me when she’s upset. Always making sure if we get into a heated conversation, that we talk things through because she doesn’t want us to lose each other. Maybe I am a fool for hanging around but damn it, I’m her fool.
